title: First exploration: broader or more central heating?
question: At fixed total heating energy, can the system find a heating profile that improves integrated simulated fusion energy, and does that improvement survive stricter checks?
description: The original six-experiment closed loop. It preserved a failed broad-heating idea and ended with incomplete verification.
limitations: Horizon is 1.0 s, shortened from the documented 5 s example.

Remaining budget is 5; this is not a verify or stop step.

payload.hypothesis: Further on-axis shift of the winning peaked Gaussian raises integrated fusion above the 111.57 MJ incumbent.
payload.prediction: E_fusion exceeds 111.57 MJ at location 0.05 and width 0.0728, with peak Ti above the 18.04 keV incumbent.
payload.rationale: Measured results: broadening width 0.0728→0.2 at baseline radius cut E_fusion by 8.63 MJ (110.36→101.74) and dropped peak Ti 16.66→14.70 keV. Shifting location 0.127→0.08 at fixed peaked width raised E_fusion by 1.21 MJ (110.36→111.57) and peak Ti to 18.04 keV. Next step isolates that winning axis by moving to the 0.05 location bound while holding the peaked width that beat the broad case. 3 of 6 experiments remain; verify is premature until this on-axis bound is measured.
